doc.title: Dave Frishberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001

title: Country-and-western songs of the mid-60s
summary: A publisher told him to write cowboy songs; they discuss the churchy III chord in one.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I love this, it’s got a certain Americana.

Glen Campbellesque, yeah I know. I was trying to write that way. I was trying to write like — I don’t know what you call it, we call it country & western or whatever. This was the middle 60s and you know I was starting to write songs and I figured I might as well try to write for the market. And this was the market part of it. The publisher actually said to me, “I like these, these are nice songs and everything and they’re very funny and very nice, but you know, why don’t you go home and write some country-western stuff. Write a cowboy song.”
“Write some cowboy songs, I can get you some records.” So I went home and I wrote some. This is not the only one, I wrote maybe a half a dozen of them. But I like this one.
Yeah, I love this song. This chord change — same thing that’s in “Georgia,” isn’t it? Like the one to the major three or something?
Well it’s the three chord, yeah.
It’s got a character to it.
It’s very churchy and it sounds like Bach harmony. I mean yeah, it’s Theory I is what it
